title: The Garage Fire That Sent Chung Ju-yung Back to His Moneylender
conflicts: Year of the garage takeover: 1940 (Asan museum, Jeon/Segye, Lankov/Korea Times) vs 1941 (Hyundai Motor Europe); used 1940. Vehicles burned: five trucks and an Oldsmobile (museum) vs three trucks and an Oldsmobile plus two half-burned (Jeon); story says 'several trucks'. Purchase money: 3,500 won (Jeon) vs a 3,000 won loan (Wikipedia, not cited); no figure given. 1943: forced merger (museum, Hyundai Europe) vs closed without compensation (Lankov); story says forced merger, after which he lost it.
notes: English sources on the fire itself are thin: the pivotal detail rests on the Asan Chung Ju-yung Museum's official biography and Jeon Young-sun's Korean-language Segye Ilbo column (loads, but the checker cannot see Chung's name in Latin script). The cause of the fire, the 1,000 won second loan and the Sinseol-dong shed are attributed to Jeon in the text. Chung's autobiography has a chapter on the fire but only its contents page was readable, so no words of his about it are quoted.
